Q9. The phenomenon of mirage is due to
(a) Increased absorption of light by air at higher
temperature
(b) Change in the refractive index of air with the
change in temperature
(c) Total internal reflection
(d) Decreased absorption of light by air at higher
temperature
The correct option is (b).
     • A mirage occurs because layers of air at
         different temperatures have different
         densities, thus different refractive indices.
     • Light rays bend (refract) when passing
         through these layers; on hot surfaces the
         refractive index gradient can bend rays
                   UPSC PYQs - 1989                             •   Hence, option (b) is correct.

Q10. The speed of light will be minimum while                   • Hence, option (c) is correct.
passing through
(a) glass
(b) vacuum
(c) water
(d) air
The correct option is (a).
     • Speed of light in a medium is 𝑐/𝑛, where n is
         the refractive index. Higher n → lower speed.
     • Approximate refractive indices: vacuum = 1.0,
         air ≈ 1.0003, water ≈ 1.33, glass ≈ 1.5.
     • Glass has the highest refractive index among
         the options, so light travels slowest in glass.
     • Hence, option (a) is correct.

        and medieval scholars had ideas about
        gravity.
     • The 7th-century Indian mathematician and
        astronomer Brahmagupta wrote in his text,
        the Brahmasphutasiddhanta, that "all things
        fall to the earth by a law of nature, for it is the
        nature of the earth to attract and keep
        things."
     • This statement is a remarkable early
        description of gravity as an attractive
        property of the Earth, anticipating Newton's
        concept by over a thousand years, although it
        lacked the mathematical formulation and               Q9. Suppose a rocketship is receding from the Earth

Q7. The known forces of nature can be divided into                  Select the correct answer using the code
four classes, viz, gravity, electromagnetism, weak                  given below:
nuclear force and strong nuclear force. With                        (a) 1 only
reference to them, which one of the following                       (b) 2 and 3 only
statements is not correct?                                          (c) 1 and 3 only
(a) Gravity is the strongest of the four.                           (d) 1, 2, and 3
(b) Electromagnetism acts only on particles with an        The correct option is (d).
electric charge.                                           Explanation:
•   Tides are the periodic rise and fall of sea        •   Hence, option (d) is correct.
    levels, caused by the combined effects of
    gravitational and rotational forces acting on
    Earth’s oceans.
•   Gravitational Force of the Sun:
        o The Sun’s gravity exerts a tidal pull on
             Earth’s oceans, producing solar tides.
        o Though the Sun is very far away, its
             large mass allows it to influence
             ocean waters measurably.
•   Gravitational Force of the Moon:
        o The Moon, being closer to Earth,
             exerts a stronger gravitational pull
             than the Sun.
        o It creates lunar tides, which are more
             than twice as strong as solar tides.
        o The side of Earth facing the Moon
             experiences a tidal bulge due to this
             gravitational attraction.
•   Centrifugal Force of the Earth:
        o The Earth–Moon system rotates
             around a common center of mass
             (the barycenter).
        o This creates a centrifugal force that
             pushes water outward on the side
             opposite the Moon, forming a second
             tidal bulge.
        o This is why most coastal regions
             experience two high tides and two
             low tides per day.
•   The alignment of the Sun, Moon, and Earth
    affects tide intensity:
        o Spring Tides: During new and full
             moons, the Sun and Moon align,
             combining their gravitational forces to
             produce higher high tides and lower
             low tides.
        o Neap Tides: During quarter moons,
             the Sun and Moon act at right angles,
             partially cancelling each other’s
             effects, resulting in weaker tides.
•   Therefore, all three factors — solar gravity,
    lunar gravity, and the centrifugal force due to
    Earth’s rotation — contribute to the
    occurrence of tides.
